# CodeDAC

> CodeDAC is an independent developer of small utility apps for Android and Windows — floating tools that stay on top of other apps (notes, timers, calculator, crypto ticker, reading guide, clipboard), plus auto start, volume boost and on-device photo redaction. Every app is free to download with an optional Pro upgrade; pages are available in 21 languages.

## Android apps (Google Play)

- [Clipboard+](https://codedac.com/apps/clipboard.html): Clipboard history & manager. Copy, save, search and paste on phone or PC. Key features: Optional Auto-save keeps what you copy the moment you copy it; text and images in a searchable history, newest first; Resizable floating overlay for use over any app; Organize frequent text into snippets and groups; Instant search and filter by keyword, text, image, or date; Fast paste from a home screen widget and the notification panel, and save from any app via the text selection menu; Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive, export clipboard history to PDF, plus backup and restore. Free vs Pro: Free keeps your text and image clipboard history with search, snippets, up to 3 groups, the floating panel, the widget and the selection-menu shortcut, and it shows ads. Pro removes the ads and adds phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive, unlimited image clips, the expanded floating panel and widget, unlimited groups, PDF export and backup restore — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.clipboard
- [AutoStart+](https://codedac.com/apps/autostart.html): Auto-launch your apps on boot. No root required, set once. Key features: Auto starts your selected apps after every reboot, as soon as you unlock the phone — no root, no custom ROM; Car Mode for head units: your apps open again every time the screen wakes from sleep — free; Drag the rows to decide which app starts first at every boot; Launch delay (PRO): wait a few seconds before the first app and space the rest apart, so car head units and slow devices finish starting up first; Run now from any row's ⋮ menu — check your list without rebooting the phone; After a reboot, a banner starts your whole list in one tap as soon as you unlock the phone (PRO); Free auto starts 1 app; PRO lifts the limit and launches your whole list in order. Free vs Pro: The free version starts 1 app per boot. PRO removes the limit, so the whole list launches in the order you set. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.autostart
- [FloatCalc+](https://codedac.com/apps/floatcalc.html): A floating calculator with FX and unit converters, on top of any app. Key features: Floats over any app — YouTube, maps, browser, banking, shopping, documents — and reopens in the mode you used last; The usual calculator keypad with a live result as you type; long-press % for ^ and ÷ for √; Select a number in any app and tap “Calculate with FloatCalc+”; copy and paste from the ⋮ menu, or long-press the result to copy it; Unit and currency converters on the same keypad: length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed and time, plus daily ECB rates for 30+ currencies; Open it from the Quick Settings tile, a home screen widget or the notification buttons; Shrink the panel to an icon docked at the screen edge, or let it shrink by itself; large keys, key vibration, adjustable opacity and 8 themes, with the default theme following dark mode. Free vs Pro: The floating calculator, length units, currency conversion between your own currency, USD and EUR, your last 5 calculations, 3 opacity steps and the default theme are free, with ads. Pro removes the ads and adds every unit category and currency pair, up to 100 history entries, 7 more themes and fine control of opacity, size and width — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatcalc
- [FloatCrypto+](https://codedac.com/apps/floatcrypto.html): A live crypto ticker floating over any app, with alerts and charts. Key features: Floating price ticker on top of every app — drag it anywhere, resize it, dial the opacity down; Price alerts on an upper or lower target, added straight from the coin card with the coin filled in; Watchlist of the coins you care about, with live price, 24-hour change and drag-to-reorder; 1-day / 7-day / 30-day charts with period high, low, open and change; Eastern and Western color modes — green-up/red-down, or red-up/blue-down as read in Korea, Japan and China; Binance prices with an automatic fallback source, delayed by up to 30 seconds (10 on Pro). Free vs Pro: Free follows 2 coins with 1 price alert and the 1-day chart, with ads. Pro gives up to 10 coins, unlimited alerts, 7-day and 30-day charts, a 10-second refresh instead of 30 seconds and no ads — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatcrypto
- [FloatTimer+](https://codedac.com/apps/floattimer.html): A floating timer, counter and stopwatch that stays over any app. Key features: Floating overlay — timers, counters, and stopwatches float on any app; drag them anywhere and set size, opacity, and background color per item; Multi-timer — any hours/minutes/seconds countdown, with 1, 5, 10, 25, 30 and 60-minute quick presets and as many timers running at once as you like; a home screen widget floats and starts any timer in one tap; Overlay controls — play, pause, and reset right on the floating timer, with a bar for the time left; drag it onto the X to close it, or collapse it to a bubble marked with the app icon and tap anywhere on it to open it again; Tally counter — tap to count up or down right on the overlay, with a step of 1, 2, 5, or 10 and as many counters as you need; Stopwatch — several stopwatches, each timed separately; start, pause, and reset without leaving your current app; Alerts and backup — sound, vibration, or a full-screen alert when time is up, plus file export and restore that merges or replaces. Free vs Pro: Unlimited timers, counters and stopwatches with sound and vibration alerts, plus the home screen widget. The free version shows two floating timers at a time; Pro adds a full-screen alert even with the screen off, your own alarm sound and vibration, auto-repeat, as many floating timers at once as you like, and no ads. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floattimer
- [VolumeBooster+](https://codedac.com/apps/volumebooster.html): Volume booster and equalizer — one tap to 150%, up to 225%, and your device volume comes up with it. Key features: One-tap levels 100%, 125%, 150% and Max: each raises your device volume, then boosts most apps up to 225% (+15 dB) — 183% free, 225% with Pro; Device volume slider right on the main screen, and the volume buttons control your device volume — so a low phone volume never hides the boost; Loudness Maximizer with multiband compression, makeup gain and an always-on peak limiter — louder, with no clipping; Equalizer tab with a 5-band equalizer and 9 presets, all free, plus Bass Booster, 3D Virtualizer and AutoEQ — 2,456 measured headphone profiles, mainstream brands (Apple, Samsung, Sony, Bose, JBL, Beats) free; Floating panel over any app with the same levels in its menu, hearing protection stats (Pro), a sleep timer with fade-out, L/R balance, a Quick Settings tile, a home-screen widget and notification controls; Safe, Caution and Danger colors based on WHO hearing guidance show how far you have pushed the volume. Free vs Pro: Free gives you up to 183% (+10 dB), all 9 presets, the 5-band equalizer, the floating panel and AutoEQ for mainstream brands like Apple, Samsung, Sony, Bose, JBL and Beats, with ads. Pro unlocks 225% (+15 dB), every AutoEQ profile and the hearing protection dashboard, and removes the ads — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.volumebooster
- [PhotoCleaner+](https://codedac.com/apps/photocleaner.html): Hide personal info in photos & PDFs, fully on-device. Key features: Solid opaque mask that can't be recovered (not a blur or mosaic); Draw masks by hand, then move, resize or delete them, with zoom for precision; Built-in detection suggests likely sensitive text (ID numbers, cards, phones, emails) — free and unlimited, as a starting point you review; Mask photos, ID cards and multi-page PDF documents; Zero permissions, an EXIF & GPS notice, and every saved or shared copy re-encoded with no EXIF; No watermark for anyone: 3 exports a day on free, unlimited with Pro along with PDF export and printing. Free vs Pro: Three times a day. What counts is the Export button, whatever you do with the result: save, share, PDF or print. Detection, editing and masking are never capped. Pro removes the daily limit. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.photocleaner
- [ReadFocus+](https://codedac.com/apps/readfocus.html): A dyslexia & ADHD reading aid with line highlight & mask. Key features: Line Highlight (Reading Ruler): illuminates your current line to keep eyes on track; Reading Mask: dims everything except your reading zone for tunnel-vision focus; Fully adjustable focus strip: height (50dp–300dp) and opacity (10%–100%); 10 color themes (3 free + 7 Pro); Works on top of any app — ebooks, PDF, webtoons, news, research papers; Pro: no ads, 7 more color themes, and keep screen on while reading. Free vs Pro: Yes. The free version includes both focus modes, 3 color themes and strip height and opacity adjustment, with ads. Pro removes the ads and adds 7 more color themes and Keep Screen On — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.readfocus
- [FloatNote+](https://codedac.com/apps/floatnote.html): Sticky notes that float over any app. Collapse to a chip, expand to a card, with colors and rich text. Key features: Floating overlay notes: collapse a note to a chip, expand it to a full card over any app; 7 sticky-note colors and rich text: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color and size; Inline images (Pro): attach photos right inside a note; Note reminders — once, every day, weekdays or chosen days; Library with instant search, pinning and drag-to-reorder — dragging a chip to the bottom zone stashes the note instead of deleting it; Pro: unlimited floating notes, inline images, Google Drive sync, unlimited reminders, no ads. Free vs Pro: Yes. Saving notes is unlimited and free, and the free version floats one note at a time and gives you all 7 colors, adjustable opacity, export and import and the home screen widget, with ads. Pro adds unlimited floating notes, inline images, Google Drive sync and unlimited reminders, and removes ads. Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatnote

## Windows apps (Microsoft Store)

- [Clipboard+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/clipboardwin.html): A Windows tray clipboard manager that syncs with the Clipboard+ Android app. Key features: Sits in the tray and saves text and images the moment you copy them — it never has to keep checking in the background, so it stays light; Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive; Android-style UI with light/dark themes, group sidebar, snippets, and pin/copy/edit/search; Multi-select bulk move, delete, and merge, newest/oldest sorting, and a full-size image viewer; Quick-pick popup at the cursor on a global hotkey, plus hotkeys to open the window and capture text selected in other apps, and run-at-startup; Export/import compatible with the Android Clipboard+ backup format, plus PDF export. Free vs Pro: The clipboard history, snippets and groups, search, the quick-pick popup, and the light and dark themes are all free. Pro adds Google Drive sync, copying image clips back to the clipboard, PDF export, backup import, unlimited groups, and unlimited image storage — free image storage is capped at 50 MB. Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9N9SRKQV1R6D
- [ReadFocus+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/readfocuswin.html): A click-through focus strip for Windows — Mask and Highlight keep your eyes on the line. Key features: Two reading modes — Mask dims everything outside a clear band, Highlight marks the line you are on; Click-through: keep scrolling, selecting and clicking the app underneath — nothing intercepts your mouse; A floating panel to switch mode, move or lock the strip and hide it, collapsing to a single row when you do not need it; Keyboard shortcuts for start and stop, mode, show and hide, lock, and nudging the strip up or down; Multi-monitor: the reading band follows the panel to whichever screen you move it to, and waits in the system tray until you need it; No ads. Pro is a one-time purchase: premium themes and Keep Screen On. Free vs Pro: Yes. The free version includes both reading modes, Focus Strip height and opacity, and three of the ten themes. Pro is a one-time purchase — not a subscription — and adds premium themes and Keep Screen On. The Windows version has no ads. Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NMSHKKX3R5C
- [FloatNote+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/floatnotewin.html): Sticky notes that float over any window on Windows, syncing with the FloatNote+ Android app. Key features: Sticky notes that float above every window: a chip expands into an editable card in place, and Esc folds it back; Never steals focus — drag or click a chip and your cursor stays in the app you were typing in; Note reminders — once, every day, weekdays or chosen days; Rich text — bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color and size — with 7 pastel note colors and inline images; Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive — the same app-private folder the Android app uses, and never a CodeDAC server; Global hotkeys, system tray, light and dark themes, run at logon, 21 languages. No ads, and every feature is free. Free vs Pro: Yes. Every feature of the Windows version is free — as many floating notes as you like, inline images, note transparency, Google Drive sync, and export and import. No in-app purchases, no ads, no account. (On the phone side, sync is a Pro feature of the Android app.) Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NW6610397TC
- [FloatTimer+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/floattimerwin.html): Timers, counters and stopwatches that float over any window on Windows as small pastel cards. Key features: Timers, counters and stopwatches float above every window as small pastel cards — drag one anywhere, resize it, or collapse it to a bubble marked with the app icon; Never steals focus — click or drag a card and your cursor stays in the document you were typing in; Start, pause and reset from the card itself without opening the app; counters add and subtract with a click on either half; Nine pastel colors, adjustable card size and opacity, and app windows that follow your light or dark theme; The backup file is the same format as the Android app, so you can export on one and restore on the other; Global hotkeys, system tray, run at logon, 21 languages. No account, no network, no ads — and Pro is a one-time purchase. Free vs Pro: Yes. You can make as many timers, counters and stopwatches as you like — the list is never limited — and the Windows version has no ads. The free version floats one card on screen at a time. Pro is a one-time purchase — not a subscription — and adds unlimited floating cards, repeating timers, any color you like, and your own alert sound or a full-screen alert. Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P3CTX3SXTGW
- [PhotoCleaner+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/photocleanerwin.html): Hide personal info in photos, screenshots and PDFs on your PC before you share. Key features: Finds phone numbers, emails, card numbers, IBAN, passport numbers and MRZ, Korean IDs, names, addresses, license plates, faces and QR codes; Review every box before export: click to toggle, drag to move, drag an edge to resize, draw your own, Undo any step; Open photos, screenshots and PDFs by drag and drop, Ctrl+V, or right-click "Clean with PhotoCleaner+" in File Explorer; Solid, opaque masks — not a blur — and no watermark; Save as JPEG or PNG, Copy, Share, Save PDF and Print; Saved copies carry no EXIF, GPS location or other metadata, and your original is never overwritten; Fully on your PC: no account, no upload, no recent-files list. Light and dark theme, 21 languages. Free vs Pro: Finding personal info is free and unlimited, and you can save, copy or share the masked copy of 3 documents a day for free. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes the daily limit and adds PDF export, printing, the always-hide list and your choice of mask color. There are no ads and no watermark, on either version. Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P22XH3N66VM
- [FloatCrypto+ for Windows](https://codedac.com/apps/floatcryptowin.html): A live crypto price ticker that floats over every window on Windows, with price alerts and charts. Key features: A live price ticker on top of every window — drag it anywhere, adjust opacity and text size, or collapse it into a bubble at the screen edge; Never steals focus — the ticker stays visible while your cursor stays in the app you are working in; Price alerts above or below a target, one-time or repeating, added straight from a coin's ⋮ menu with the coin already picked; Watchlist from the hundreds of Binance pairs, drag-to-reorder, and 1-day, 7-day and 30-day charts with period high, low, open and change; Western (green up, red down) or Eastern (red up, blue down) colors, and a full price table on the tray icon; Global hotkeys, system tray, start with Windows, light and dark themes, 21 languages. No ads, no account. Free vs Pro: Free follows 2 coins with 1 price alert, refreshes every 30 seconds and shows the 1-day chart — and the ticker has no time limit. Pro is a one-time purchase that raises this to 10 coins, unlimited alerts, a 10-second refresh and the 7-day and 30-day charts. The Windows version has no ads. Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NMFCT755G24

## Guides

- [How to see your clipboard history on Android](https://codedac.com/guides/android-clipboard-history.html): Android keeps only the last thing you copied. Here is where to find recent clips in your keyboard, and how to keep a searchable history that does not disappear.
- [How to open an app automatically after a reboot on Android (no root)](https://codedac.com/guides/open-app-automatically-after-reboot-android.html): Android has no setting that launches an app when the phone starts. Here is how to make your apps open by themselves after a restart, without root — and how to test it without rebooting.
- [How to keep a note on top of other apps on Android](https://codedac.com/guides/floating-notes-over-other-apps-android.html): Keep a note visible while you use another app: a floating note that stays over any app, folds into a small chip, and can pop up at a time you choose.
- [How to keep a timer on screen while using other apps on Android](https://codedac.com/guides/floating-timer-over-other-apps-android.html): The Clock app's timer disappears when you switch apps. Here is how to keep a countdown, stopwatch or counter floating over any app.
- [How to hide personal info in a screenshot before you share it](https://codedac.com/guides/hide-personal-info-in-screenshots.html): Blur, a light pen or a highlighter can leave text readable. Here is how to cover phone numbers, card numbers and faces so they can't be recovered — on your phone, without uploading anything.
- [How to keep a sticky note always on top on Windows](https://codedac.com/guides/sticky-notes-always-on-top-windows.html): Notes on the desktop end up behind the window you are working in. Here is how to pin a note on top of every window — with PowerToys, or with notes that float by design.
- [How to see your clipboard history on Windows](https://codedac.com/guides/clipboard-history-windows.html): Windows has a built-in clipboard history (Win+V), but it is short and is cleared when you restart. Here is how to use it, and how to keep a searchable history that lasts.
- [How to keep a timer on top of other windows on Windows](https://codedac.com/guides/timer-always-on-top-windows.html): Keep a countdown visible while you work in other windows — with the Clock app's "Keep on top", or with timers that float as small cards over everything.
- [Reading ruler for dyslexia and ADHD on Android: keep your place while reading](https://codedac.com/guides/reading-ruler-dyslexia-adhd-android.html): Losing the line, skipping rows or re-reading the same sentence? A reading ruler or reading mask over any app helps your eyes stay on track. Here is how to set one up on Android.
- [How to use a reading ruler on Windows (for dyslexia and ADHD)](https://codedac.com/guides/reading-ruler-windows.html): Edge's Immersive Reader has Line focus for web pages. For PDFs, documents and every other app, a click-through focus strip keeps your eyes on the line. Here is how to use both.
- [How to use a calculator on top of other apps on Android](https://codedac.com/guides/floating-calculator-over-other-apps-android.html): Work out a discount or convert a price without leaving your shopping, banking or browser screen: a floating calculator that stays over any app, with unit and currency converters.
- [How to see crypto prices while using other apps on Android](https://codedac.com/guides/crypto-price-ticker-over-other-apps-android.html): Keep a live crypto ticker on screen while you watch videos, read or chat, and get notified when a coin crosses your target price.
- [How to make your Android phone louder](https://codedac.com/guides/make-android-phone-louder.html): Phone too quiet even at full volume? Check these settings first, then see how a volume booster raises your device volume and boosts most apps in one tap.
- [How to hide personal info in screenshots and PDFs on Windows](https://codedac.com/guides/hide-personal-info-in-screenshots-windows.html): Before you share a screenshot or a scanned document from your PC, cover phone numbers, card numbers, IDs and faces with solid masks — without uploading anything.
- [How to keep a live crypto ticker on top of other windows on Windows](https://codedac.com/guides/crypto-price-ticker-on-top-windows.html): Watch the coins you follow while you work: a slim price ticker above every window, price alerts as desktop notifications, and charts on a double-click.
